articleTitle: Function Scheduling with Data Security in Serverless Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: In serverless computing, the service provider takes full responsibility for function management. However, serverless computing has many challenges regarding data security and function scheduling. To address these challenges, we have proposed a system to secure the data of an end-user. We also aim to meet the quality of service (QoS) for the end-user requests. This work presents a Simulated Annealing-based optimization algorithm for function placement. Also, we have Hyperledger Fabric, a blockchain framework in the system architecture for securing the data of an end-user. We have conducted experiments in Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) taking virtual machine instances. The experiments in Amazon EC2 indicate that the proposed system secures the data and enhances the end-user’s QoS.

articleTitle: mmTCP: An Adaptive Congestion Control Algorithm for 5G mmWave Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The emergence of 5G New Radio technology, especially using millimeter-wave frequencies, offers unparalleled data rates and low latency, which are crucial for the new generation. However, the limited range of high-frequency bands, such as mmWave and TeraHertz, results in frequent channel quality fluctuations and handoffs. Additionally, urban micro-cellular deployments encounter frequent channel variations and outages due to UE (vehicle) mobility, making it challenging for TCP protocols to adapt to fluctuating link quality and network capacity. This often results in underutilized resources, service disruptions, and connectivity gaps. To address these issues, we introduce mmTCP—a solution that dynamically adjusts the congestion window based on signal quality post-handoff to minimize delay and maximize throughput, enabling the transport layer to adapt to shifting wireless conditions. mmTCP optimizes congestion and flow control to mitigate link fluctuations and enhance user experience. ns-3 experiments show that mmTCP consistently improves throughput by up to 42% and reduces latency by up to 43% through effective link-layer adaptations in Numerology 2.

articleTitle: Performance of DVQKD Protocol Over Gamma Gamma Turbulence Channel
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the performance of a discrete variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD) system over a turbulence channel under moderate to strong turbulence conditions. We employ the Gamma-Gamma turbulence model for the turbulence channel and derive analytical expressions for the average quantum bit error rate (QBER) and secrecy key rate (SKR) of the decoy state DV-QKD protocol. Both analytical and numerical simulation results demonstrate that, for the decoy-state QKD protocol, the QBER of the FSO system highly depends on the link length but is largely unaffected by turbulence strength. Furthermore, the numerical simulation results reveal that the SKR remains stable even under stronger turbulence.

articleTitle: PyBlkSim: An Open-Source Block-Based Discrete-Time Simulator
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: PyBlkSim is a block-based simulator developed for discrete-time simulations. PyBlkSim is useful for simulating a wide range of real-world discrete-time systems including systems belonging to signal processing and communications domains. PyBlkSim is written in Python and built using Python’s discreteevent simulation library, SimPy. PyBlkSim blocks use popular Python libraries such as NumPy and SciPy, which have been tried and tested extensively for various scientific computing applications. In its current form, PyBlkSim supports several blocks, ranging from different signal sources and sinks to filters, math, and signal operations. The simulator and its accompanying blocks are open-sourced, allowing developers to edit and extend the code to suit their needs. PyBlkSim differs from its counterparts, such as GNU Radio and Simulink, in that it is open-source, supports multiple operating systems, and can natively incorporate Python scientific libraries in its blocks. In this paper, we discuss the need for PyBlkSim, its design framework, the structure of its blocks and the characterization of its performance. As an example, we also demonstrate the use of PyBlkSim to simulate an On-Off Keying (OOK) modulation and demodulation scheme.

articleTitle: A Game-Theoretic Approach for Cost-Effective and Reliable Task Offloading in Fog-enabled IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Most applications today rely on the Internet of Things (IoT), which generates several tasks to be processed. Since IoT devices have limited processing capacity, processing these tasks locally is challenging. Therefore, Fog-enabled IoT networks, known as FC-IoT, are ideally suited for processing these tasks while enhancing the quality of service (QoS). In a heterogeneous FC-IoT, the state of fog nodes may vary at different times based on workload, and sometimes they may also fail. This requires a reliable and cost-effective task-offloading approach that can adapt smoothly as fog node conditions change. This article introduces a reliable and cost-effective task offloading strategy for FC-IoT networks that can model dynamic pricing interactions with Stackelberg game theory between fog nodes and IoT devices. In this model, the fog nodes take the role of leader that adjusts the cost according to their states. Meanwhile, IoT devices act as followers that select a fog node according to the observed cost and reliability. We analyzed real-time fog node reliability using a Continuous-Time Markov Chain (CTMC), capturing the state transitions, failures, and recovery rates. Additionally, we incorporate Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) to efficiently manage energy consumption, balancing processing demands with power requirements. The simulation results show that our model reduces energy consumption while maintaining reliable task offloading at a minimal cost.

articleTitle: LP-GRU Model: A Graph Analytics Approach to Detect Misinformation Infiltrators in Online Communities
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Fighting the propagation of misinformation within a social media group or community by focusing on identifying dishonest members who deliberately try to quash any constructive social movement is very challenging because such people use advanced tactics to create division and doubt by manipulating information. The present research aims to develop a hybrid heuristic model to identify those who intentionally spread misleading information on social media to jeopardize a social movement. We frame this issue under the heading of Graph Semi-supervised Learning (GSSL), and we propose a hybrid model that falls under the heuristic approach, called Label Propagation-Gated Recurrent Unit (LP-GRU). LP-GRU can effectively identify perpetrators of disinformation within social communities by fusing community structure from the Label Propagation algorithm with behavioral patterns identified by GRU. Compared to previous heuristic approaches, we achieve up to 76% accuracy when using the LP-GRU model on augmented semi-synthetic social network data.

articleTitle: Pilot-Enhanced RNN-Aided Channel Estimation for Vehicular Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Accurate wireless channel estimation (CE) is essential for vehicular communication networks, where high mobility poses significant challenges. Deep Learning (DL) enhanced Data-pilot-aided (DPA) techniques improve CE by employing channel prediction through Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) using past channel estimates. However, existing RNN-based CE methods rely solely on previous estimates, neglecting the useful information in current pilots. To address this limitation, we propose the Pilot-Enhanced RNN-Aided DPA (PERA-DPA) scheme, which integrates current and previous pilot estimates to better capture dynamic channel variations. Using a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network, PERA-DPA achieves superior estimation accuracy in high-mobility environments. Simulations show that PERA-DPA outperforms GRU-DPA-TA with a 2 dB SNR gain at a BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>. Implementation on an ARM Cortex A9 processor demonstrates that this performance improvement comes at only a 4% increase in computational latency, making PERA-DPA a promising solution for channel estimation in vehicular systems under high-mobility conditions.

articleTitle: ZTAAC : Zero Trust Adaptive Authorization with CP-ABE for Context-Aware Data Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: In modern dynamic and distributed computing environments, secure and adaptive access control for sensitive data is essential. Traditional access control models often fail to address the complexities of evolving and heterogeneous systems. To overcome these challenges, we propose a Zero Trust Adaptive Authorization Architecture (ZTAAC) that integrates the principles of Zero Trust, Never trust, always verify, along with the cryptographic flexibility of a Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (CP-ABE) scheme. ZTAAC introduces a central zero trust controller, which incorporates a policy decision point and a risk engine to facilitate real-time risk assessment and dynamic policy enforcement. The risk engine evaluates contextual parameters such as user location, device posture, and behaviour patterns to enable real-time adaptation of access policies through feedback loops that refine access decisions dynamically. Our enhanced CP-ABE framework embeds static and dynamic attributes-based access policies within encrypted data, ensuring that only authorized users with valid context can decrypt it. Dynamic attribute management facilitates the generation and integration of key components for contextual attributes and aligns access decisions with current security postures. Preliminary performance analysis confirms ZTAAC’s scalability and efficiency, establishing it as a robust and adaptive solution for securing data in next-generation cloud-assisted and distributed environments.

articleTitle: Intelligent Cost-Effective Electric Vehicle Charging Solutions for Cities and Highway Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: In this work, we address the strategic placement and optimal sizing of electric vehicle charging stations for cities as well as highway traffic to minimize overall cost. We formulate the problem as a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model and propose a set of greedy algorithms to obtain scalable solutions quickly. For city areas, we propose a systematic approach considering factors like population density and traffic patterns to maximize customer satisfaction and minimize costs. For highways and expressways, we account for deterministic inter-arrival times and maximum waiting times. Additionally, we propose an integrated approach that, when run for two cities and a connecting highway, demonstrates a total cost reduction compared to using separate algorithms for cities and highways.

articleTitle: Eyes on You: TinyML-Powered On-Device Face Tracking for Low-Cost, Low-Power, Secure MCU Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, low-power face-tracking system utilizing TinyML, designed for real-time face detection and tracking on an ESP32-CAM board. The system employs two servo motors for pan and tilt adjustments, ensuring that detected faces remain within the camera’s view. Operating entirely on-device, the system prioritizes privacy by eliminating the need for network access. It utilizes a multitask learning model that both classifies the presence of a human face with 96% accuracy and predicts the corresponding bounding box coordinates, achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.65 for precise face tracking. Optimized for low-power microcontroller units (MCUs), the model has hardware requirements of 103 KB RAM, 323 KB Flash, and 7.5 million MAC operations, enabling inference times of 850 ms on the ESP32-CAM and 150 ms on the Teensy 4.1. To address the lack of publicly available datasets for single-face tracking in resource-constrained settings, a custom dataset derived from the COCO-Faces and Visual Wake Words datasets was created and published on Zenodo, accessible at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14474899. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work demonstrating real-time face tracking in MCU environments, with a detection range of up to 2.5 meters, offering a low-resource footprint and high accuracy. This contribution supports advancements in low-power face-tracking applications for IoT security, interactive displays, and human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Missing Value Imputation for IoT data: With Applications to Reefer Container Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This research presents adaptive imputation methods for handling missing Internet of Things (IoT) data, specifically in reefer container monitoring. It proposes an enhanced Vector Auto-Regressive (VAR) model for real-time adaptability, a two-stage framework to address non-stationary data, a time-varying kernel-based weighting scheme to consider time-varying dependencies among variables, and a modified Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to further improve imputation accuracy for noisy training data. Validated on real-world datasets, these models demonstrate superior performance, operational efficiency, and decision-making capability, paving the way for efficient edge deployment in IoT enabled cold chain monitoring systems.

articleTitle: TGNN-Bet: Approximation of Temporal Betweenness Centrality using Temporal Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Networks appear across various domains, and identifying central nodes in temporal networks is more challenging than in static networks. Temporal betweenness centrality is the widely used method to assess the importance of the nodes. This method is based on shortest temporal path calculations. However, computing this centrality metrics value is computationally intensive, especially for large-scale networks. Various approximation algorithms exist, but they often lack efficiency or accuracy. We introduce TGNN-Bet, a temporal graph neural network model, to approximate temporal betweenness centrality. In TGNN-Bet, each node gathers features from multi-hop neighbors, enabling the model to simulate paths and capture the reachability of nodes. The model’s effectiveness is validated using the Spearman correlation (ρ) performance metric and comparing system runtimes with the existing temporal betweenness centrality method. Experimental results on six real-world temporal networks demonstrate that TGNN-Bet strongly correlates with existing temporal betweenness centrality methods. The proposed TGNN-Bet model achieves an average computation time reduction of 94.216% compared to conventional temporal betweenness centrality methods.

articleTitle: Use of Agent-based Modeling to Gauge Impact of Lockdown Strategies on Spread of COVID-19 on an Educational Campus
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic brought unprecedented challenges to education in India, which resulted from widespread closures of colleges and schools. These closures were aimed to curb the spread of the virus among students, faculty, and staff. However, they caused significant disruptions to education. This paper uses agent-based modeling simulations to explore the dynamics of disease spread on the campuses. Our study aims to provide insights to enhance preparedness and response capabilities for future outbreaks by analyzing various scenarios and testing the effectiveness of those intervention strategiesWe consider restrictions of making zones in hostels, batches in classes, and batches in messes, aka food courts, to delay infection surges. Using quarantine reduces infections further. We find that the percentage of cumulative infections reduced from 100% in the case of free movement to 45% in the case of restricted movement with quarantine. The percentage of active infections reduced from 99% in the case of free movement to 36.6% in the case of restricted movement with quarantine. The rate of change of infections significantly reduces from 1946% and 1606% in the case of free and restricted movement, respectively, to 353% and 383% in the case of free with quarantine and restricted movement with quarantine, respectively, indicating the effectiveness of restrictions and quarantine in managing infection rates.

articleTitle: DyPSS: Dynamic Priority Signalling System for Emergency Vehicles using Fog and YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Efficient navigation of emergency response vehicles (ERVs) through urban congestion is crucial to life-saving efforts, yet traditional traffic systems often slow down their swift passage. In this work, we introduce Dynamic Priority Signalling System (DyPSS), an intelligent, multi-layered traffic management solution designed to minimize ERV delays by creating "green corridors" at traffic signals. Using technologies like fog computing, cloud computing, global positioning system and deep learning, DyPSS adjusts traffic lights instantly to clear congestion as an ERV approaches. Simulation testing was conducted using SUMO and it demonstrated DyPSS’s potential to significantly reduce ERV travel time in dense urban settings with minimal disruption to general traffic flow. This system could drastically improve emergency response by reducing delays and helping responders reach their destinations faster, potentially saving more lives.

articleTitle: Enabling Intelligent Observability Volume Management
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: In the era of centralized clouds, multi-cloud, and edge computing, adaptable observability is essential to efficiently manage the growing volume of metrics data. Observability Volume Manager (OVM) addresses the complexities of dynamic observability data management by offering tailored processing capabilities that ensures efficient and effective observability across diverse infrastructures. This demo highlights OVM’s ability to perform dynamic transformations for fine-grained control over observability data collection, while significantly reducing the volume of data collected, processed, and stored. These optimizations drive substantial cost savings and position OVM as an essential solution for cost-efficient observability.

articleTitle: Integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial-Network Architecture for Edge Caching and Coded Delivery in 3GPP System
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The integration of Terrestrial Networks (TNs) and Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs), including satellites, is essential for enabling seamless, high-quality, and ubiquitous communication in the era beyond 5G. This paper proposes an architecture for implementing Edge Caching and Coded Delivery services within an integrated TN-NTN 3GPP system. The architecture introduces a two-level caching mechanism, with the first level located in the Satellite Network (Satellite Edge Computing) and the second level deployed in the ground-based Terrestrial Edge Data Network. It leverages the 5G Multicast Broadcast Service (MBS) with Point-to-Multipoint (PTM) delivery for efficient coded multicast transmission. Additionally, the paper discusses standardization aspects and addresses key challenges in deploying and integrating the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Demo: An RFSoC-Based Testbed for Over-the-Air Wireless Transceiver at Millimeter Wave Frequency
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The millimeter wave (mmW) frequency spectrum has been explored recently for large bandwidth communication. At these frequencies, narrow directional beams are required for communication since the signal attenuation is high due to atmospheric absorption. This work presents an AMD RFSoC and Sivers Semiconductors analog front-end based hardware testbed capable of directional communication via analog beamforming at mmW. The proposed testbed comprises orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based baseband physical layer and digital front-end on an ARM processor and field programmable gate array (FPGA), respectively, integrated with high-speed data converters of the RFSoC. The RFSoC output at sub-6GHz is integrated with a mmW multi-antenna analog-front end for over-the-air communication at 29.8 GHz. We demonstrate end-to-end communication over the air and present bit error rate (BER) analysis in the presence of radio frequency impairments and beam misalignments in real radio channels.

articleTitle: A Multi-Modal Smart Switching Based Image Transmission Using Semantic Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The conventional paradigm of communication primarily concentrates on the transmission of raw data, often disregarding its contextual meaning. However, to tackle the exponential growth in data demands along with the limited availability of transmission bandwidth, there is an increasing need to transition from Shannon’s classical information-theoretic communication to a more advanced framework centered on semantics. This work presents a multi-modal semantic-based communication method for the transmission of high-definition images aimed at optimizing the transmitted data volume while maintaining a high throughput and mean intersection over union score. To this end, two architectural models are explored: a denser ResNet-based and a lightweight U-Net-based. Depending on the required QoS and resource availability, the raw image is either semantically segmented to obtain a fine-grained, pixel-level classification of the image or represented as label semantics, which provides only a higher-level, object-based, or region-based classification prior to its transmission. The experimental results show that such an adaptive semantic image processing approach leads to around 63% reduction in the transmitted data volume without compromising on the quality of image reconstruction.

articleTitle: SlidEar: Exploring eSense in-Ear Wearable for Voice-Assisted Smart Slide Supervision
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: In corporate settings, conferences, or classrooms, an orator relies on manual slide transitions, which can disrupt their presentation flow. Presentation devices can be inaccessible due to the physical limitations of individuals, reducing engagement with the audience. Traditionally used remote-controlled wireless presenters are hand-held devices that usually require a compatible connector slot for the presentation device and partially engage one hand of the orator. To ease the hand-free presentation of slides, we introduce SlidEar, a voice-assisted smart slide supervision successfully tested on eSense in-ear wearables. SlidEar leverages voice recognition fusion with wearable sensors to facilitate seamless slide operations. It allows real-time feedback on natural language commands during the presentation of slides. Compared with conventional methods, SlidEar enhances engagement and accessibility through hand-free in-ear placement and helps the orator focus on delivering their content without any disruption or distraction. The evaluation shows promising results that improve the presentation experience profusion. SlidEar significantly reduces errors and can be widely adopted in diverse presentation scenarios.

articleTitle: TruChain: A Blockchain-based Access Control to Improve the Security of Smart Water Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Water is a significant resource in day-to-day life, and it usually requires technological association for comprehensive management. Smart Water Grids (SWG) typically use cyberphysical systems (CPS) to monitor several parameters associated with water quality and distribution, leveraging the possibility of performing remote operations. For robust architecture, remote operations rely on application-specific sensors, communication networks, edge control, and cloud computation. Needless to say, the centralized control of edge and cloud infrastructure is prone to attacks and failures, such as unauthorized access or single-point-of-failure. We propose TruChain, a Blockchain-based access control mechanism to eliminate the probability of access takeover and aggregate quorum-based validation on sensory data for transparent provenance reliability. We also provide access revocation to strengthen security by restricting access to sensitive data stored in a privately distributed cloud. We believe our solution has empirical decentralization and a verifiable authorization method by maintaining a tamper-evident, auditable trail of interactive events, building trust without third-party intervention.

articleTitle: PulmoWave: Pulmonary Disease Detection Using mmWave Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Pulmonary diseases such as Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disorder (COPD), Asthma, and Pneumonia present significant global health challenges, necessitating early and accurate diagnosis for improved outcomes. Traditional diagnostic methods, including spirometry and chest X-rays, are often costly, inaccessible in remote areas, and unsuitable for real-time monitoring. This paper proposes a novel, non-invasive sensing approach using mmWave radar (IWR1843) for pulmonary disease identification. The radar system captures subtle thoracic movements, enabling the analysis of respiratory patterns and vital signs such as respiratory rate, phase variations, and vibration-based chest motion. The proposed system was evaluated across COPD and normal subjects, demonstrating its capability to differentiate between these conditions based on respiratory parameters. This solution offers significant advantages, including cost-effectiveness, portability, and accessibility, making it suitable for clinical and remote settings. With the ability to provide real-time, detailed respiratory insights, this approach holds great promise for widespread deployment in pulmonary disease diagnosis and monitoring.

articleTitle: PResCon: Physiological Response Augmented Continuous Emotion Annotation Tool
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: We present an annotation tool designed to collect fine-grain continuous emotion ground truth labels and physiological responses as users watch different videos. In the existing literature, continuous emotion annotations are typically collected as self-reports based on the 2D Circumplex model through auxiliary devices (a joystick or similar tools) during video consumption. However, the users face challenges as they need to use an auxiliary device and rely on the Circumplex model’s valence and arousal axis without clear indication of distinct emotion labels. Therefore, to overcome these challenges, we introduce PResCon, a tool that allows to collect emotion annotations using keyboard arrow keys only (without using any auxiliary device) and guiding users towards the discrete emotions (e.g., amused, stressed, bored, relaxed) by embedding them on the Circumplex plane. The tool encompasses two major components - (a) a web interface that displays various stimuli videos and provision of collecting emotion labels (valence and arousal) by moving the keyboard arrow keys and (b) a sensor setup (based on Arduino) that allows to collect the physiological responses (heart rate and galvanic skin response) passively during video consumption. In summary, the PResCon tool facilitates research in the domain of affective computing by allowing to collect fine-grain continuous emotion annotations and the physiological responses in real-time during video consumption.

articleTitle: NURPS: NUMA- and Reliability-aware Parallelized SFC Deployment in Multi-Core Servers
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Network Function Virtualization (NFV) leverages Virtualized Network Functions (VNFs) to overcome the limitations of traditional middleboxes by using standard hardware to create Service Function Chains (SFCs) that deliver specific services. However, virtualization overhead and SFC length can contribute to increased end-to-end delay. To address this, Paral-lelized SFC (PSFC) enables the simultaneous execution of identical packets by multiple VNFs, significantly reducing delay. Most existing SFC placement approaches assume uniform treatment of all CPU cores in multi-core NFV servers, overlooking the impact of Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) architecture. Studies have shown that arbitrary VNF placement can degrade SFC performance due to resource contention within a NUMA node—specifically in the Last Level Cache (LLC) and Memory Bandwidth (MB)—and between NUMA nodes, particularly in Quick Path Interconnect (QPI) bandwidth. This paper presents NURPS, a NUMA-aware PSFC placement strategy that deploys VNFs by allocating critical resources, such as LLC and MB, across NUMA nodes to maximize performance while minimizing server usage. Furthermore, NURPS incorporates both software and hardware reliability into the VNF deployment process, ensuring stable performance under varying operational conditions. Extensive simulations demonstrate that NURPS effectively reduces the number of servers required for PSFC deployment while maintaining high reliability.

articleTitle: Efficiency Redefined: Impact of Reducing Data Acquisition Rate for Optimized TinyML in Resource-Constrained IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) enables cost-effective, privacy-focused machine learning inference on micro-controller units (MCUs) connected to sensors. For these resource-limited settings, achieving an optimized design is essential. This study examines the impact of reducing data acquisition rates on TinyML models designed for time series classification, especially in battery-powered IoT devices with tight resource constraints. By decreasing sampling frequency, we aim to lower computational requirements—such as RAM usage, energy consumption, latency, and multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations—by approximately four times while preserving classification accuracy. Experiments conducted with six benchmark datasets (UCIHAR, WISDM, PAMAP2, MHEALTH, MIT-BIH, and PTB) indicate that reduced data acquisition rates substantially lessen energy demands and computational overhead with minimal impact on accuracy. For instance, lowering the acquisition rate by 75% for the MIT-BIH and PTB datasets resulted in a 60% reduction in RAM use, 75% fewer MAC operations, 74% shorter latency, and a 70% decrease in energy consumption, all without compromising accuracy. These findings offer key insights into the deployment of optimized TinyML models in constrained environments.

articleTitle: Exploring Optimal and Suboptimal Beamforming Solutions Using Weighted Subspace-Search-VQE
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This work explores the application of a Quantum algorithm, namely Weighted Subspace-Search-Variational-Quantum-Eigensolver (SSVQE), a variant of the traditional VQE algorithm, to predict optimal as well as sub-optimal sparse array configurations for the problem of beamforming. The optimization formulation is designed to maximize the Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR), which is then reformulated into Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) representation to serve as the Hamiltonian for the weighted SSVQE algorithm. The results obtained are presented along with classically obtained SINR plots to facilitate a comparison of the sparse array configurations. Our findings indicate that the output from the quantum algorithm precisely match with the results obtained from the classical method.

articleTitle: Securing Legacy Interfaces of 5G Short Message Service Function (SMSF)
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Network Functions (NFs) in the 5th Generation (5G) mobile communication system face many security-related challenges. Usage of legacy interfaces/protocols is one of them. The Short Message Service Function (SMSF) in the 5G core is the key network function supporting the short message service (SMS) delivery over Non-Access Stratum (NAS) to User Equipment (UE). SMS over NAS is an old service, in existence since the 2nd Generation (2G) mobile communication systems. Therefore, the SMSF in 5G core may need to interface with legacy network elements/functions via non-service based (legacy) interfaces. Typically these legacy interfaces are based on Diameter and/or Mobile Application Part (MAP) protocols. It is essential to secure SMSF records and data (SMS) in transit over these legacy interfaces, as they may contain critical information such as UE identifiers, UE contexts and sensitive financial data. In this work, we present our contributions to 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP)’s Release 19 5G standards, which include the security threats security-related requirements for SMSF’s Diameter and MAP-based legacy interfaces as well as mechanisms to protect SMSF from these threats. These contributions were recently included in 3GPP 5G standards and Indian Telecom Security Assurance Requirements.

articleTitle: OFDM Signal Modulation Classification using Dilated CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Modern wireless communication systems, including Wi-Fi, LTE, and 5G, use the highly efficient digital transmission technique known as orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is a critical signal-processing technique employed in the physical layer of wireless communication systems. Its primary objective is to identify an incoming signal’s modulation type without prior knowledge at the receiver end. This letter outlines our proposed deep learning model for the modulation classification of OFDM using dilated convolution and modified residual network block which uses skip connections for better performance. This model is referred to as a modified residual dilated convolutional neural network (MRDCNN). The dataset containing 6 different modulation techniques which contain different modulation techniques for header and payload of OFDM signals with the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) range of -10 dB to 20 dB is used here. The implementation results show that the model gives an accuracy of 93.01% for overall SNRs ranging from -10 dB to 20 dB. It can achieve 98% accuracy for 0 dB SNR and can achieve 100% accuracy for SNRs higher than 4 dB. In addition, the proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art models in modulation classification in OFDM signals.

articleTitle: Sunlight to Signals: Solar Panel as Active Data Receiver
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Bridging the world with energy efficient communication using solar panels as communication receivers is an innovative step toward sustainable connectivity. This approach not only leverages renewable energy to power communication infrastructure but also enhances the efficiency and reach of networks, particularly in remote and underserved areas. Light communication offers high-speed data transfer and is cost-effective due to the vast unlicensed spectrum available. However, there is a challenge of high capacitive effect leading to sluggish switching response that limits solar panel operation to a few kbps. This paper presents the experimental validation of analog circuitry that improves the solar panel response, resulting in high-speed data transmission. The result presents a data rate of 10.7 Mbps over a solar panel with a received optical power of 0.36 mW transmitted using infrared light-emitting diodes. The fusion of solar power and communication technology presents a solution that addresses environmental concerns while fostering global connectivity, ensuring that even the most isolated regions can participate in the digital age.

articleTitle: Collaborative Deadline-sensitive Multi-task Offloading in Vehicular-Cloud Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: With the growing technological advancements in the Internet and advanced functionalities in vehicular networks, it becomes crucial to execute tasks quickly and efficiently. However, the limited onboard computational capacity and vehicle mobility make it challenging to accomplish latency-sensitive tasks efficiently. Task offloading provides a promising solution to overcome these challenges. Cloud data centers provide efficient solutions, but returning the results to the vehicles takes longer due to the large physical distance. Leveraging edge servers to execute latency-sensitive tasks provides a fast, interactive response and less transmission cost. However, in a dynamic network, vehicles will be in constant motion with varying speeds, resulting in frequent handoffs from one base station to another. Our proposed work aims to select the optimal nodes to perform binary offloading with minimum cost using the collaborative vehicular network. We use a greedy-based offloading approach to address these challenges and achieve better quality-of-service and quality-of-experience in a dynamic environment to minimize costs, delay reduction ratio, and satisfaction ratio. The proposed work outperforms the baseline by 60.44%, 53.43% in reducing total system cost, delay reduction ratio, and 36% improvement in the satisfaction ratio compared to baseline algorithms.

articleTitle: Quantum Network Routing with Heterogeneous Nodes
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Deciding a route for the transfer of quantum information (namely, qubits) on a quantum network is a significant problem that is being studied extensively. In this work, we investigate the problem of routing on a quantum network of heterogeneous nodes both with and without fidelity and timing constraints.We propose a Path Request Packet (PRP) based routing scheme for dynamically selecting a path that maximizes the overall probability of transmission success while maintaining fidelity above a threshold and adhering to time constraints. While the proposed scheme can perform suboptimally under fidelity and timing constraints, we discuss a straightforward proof of optimality in the absence of these constraints. Simulations on random graphs demonstrate that the PRP-based scheme performs better, both in terms of reliability and fidelity, than a non-trivial baseline routing algorithm.

articleTitle: Low-Complex Frame Synchronization in Narrowband OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is a widely used signal modulation technique that forms the backbone of technologies such as Long Term Evolution (LTE), 5G New Radio (NR), Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN), WiMAX, and others. Synchronization plays a crucial role in OFDM systems, as even small timing and frequency offset errors can lead to significant performance degradation. This paper presents a robust and efficient technique for estimating both timing and frequency offsets. The approach leverages a long preamble sequence distributed across multiple OFDM symbols in the frequency domain, where differential correlation is employed to detect the frame boundary. Subsequently, Sum of Squared Difference (SSD) is calculated to track the symbol boundary. Once the timing estimate is obtained, the same differential correlation values are applied to estimate the frequency offset. The proposed method demonstrates robust performance in detecting symbol boundaries, even in low Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR), moderate frequency offsets, and multipath conditions.

articleTitle: Learning-Based Sensing Mode Selection for ISAC in Intelligent Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) encompass a broad range of technologies and strategies that aim to provide innovative services relating to different modes of transport and traffic management and enable users to be better informed and make safer, more coordinated, and smarter use of transport networks. One of the main pillars of 6G technology, Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), integrates communication and sensing capabilities into a single system. ISAC can significantly enhance ITS by improving the way vehicles and infrastructure interact, leading to more efficient, safe, and sustainable transportation networks. Moreover, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) can provide aerial data to complement ground-based sensors in ITS, leading to more comprehensive traffic analyses. The synergy between UAVs, ITS and ISAC has the potential to create smarter, safer, and more efficient transportation networks. In ISAC systems, various sensing modes can be utilized to enhance the performance of both sensing and communication functions. Each mode has its specific applications, advantages, and limitations. In this work, we propose a learning based sensing mode selection for ISAC in ITS. By applying learning-based approaches to sensing mode selection in ISAC, ITS can enhance the operational effectiveness across diverse environments.

articleTitle: Patrol: An Intelligent Surveillance System for Mobile-Free Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The widespread and unauthorized use of mobile phones in no-mobile zones such as examination halls, government offices, and hospitals presents significant security, confidentiality, and productivity challenges. Traditional signal-based detection methods fail to detect phones in airplane mode or disconnected from networks, leaving critical gaps in enforcement. To address this issue, we propose "Phone Patrol," a deep learning-based system designed to detect and report unauthorized mobile phone usage. Phone Patrol uses You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5) for detecting individuals with mobile phones and You Only Look Once version 9 (YOLOv9) for face recognition, enabling identification of violators. Deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5, the system processes real-time video feeds and sends automated SMS alerts to offenders, offering a compact, standalone Internet of Things (IoT) solution. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv5 achieved a mean Average Precision at 50% Intersection over Union (mAP50) score of 0.992, showcasing its accuracy in detecting mobile phones. Although the current prototype has limitations in scalability and optimization for larger environments, it presents a robust proof-of-concept for image-based detection independent of network signals, providing a more comprehensive solution to enforce no-mobile zones effectively.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Discovery Framework for Maritime Intelligence on Dark Vessels
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Maritime Intelligence is essential for safeguarding maritime interests of coastal nations. Traditionally, vessel movements are tracked using self-reported positions via Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders. However, vessels engaged in illicit activities often disable their AIS transponders to evade detection, thereby going dark. Satellite-based sensors, such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) can be used to detect Dark Vessels. However, extraction of actionable insights for maritime intelligence on Dark Vessels is posed with several challenges. The spatial estimation of activities of vessels over various time periods is complicated due to spatial and temporal overlaps in satellite scans. This poster presents our ideas on knowledge discovery framework that integrates spatial analytics methods to gain actionable insights on Dark Vessels. Preliminary results are shown on Global Fishing Watch (GFW) Dataset of Dark Vessels.

articleTitle: GenCPruneX: Adaptive Channel-wise Pruning for Efficient TinyML Deployment with Genetic Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Deploying deep learning (DL) models in resource-constrained TinyML environments requires careful optimization to balance accuracy, memory, computation, and energy efficiency. Neural network pruning, a vital optimization technique, removes insignificant neurons and filters, enabling efficient deployment on edge devices. While existing open-source tools like TensorFlow Lite focus on unstructured pruning by zeroing out weights, this approach often fails to reduce inference-time resource usage on general-purpose processors, making structured pruning essential for removing entire filters or neurons. This paper presents GenCPruneX, an open-source structured pruning tool tailored to optimize deep learning models for efficient deployment in resource-limited environments. Using an L1 norm-based importance metric, GenCPruneX prunes channels in convolutional layers and neurons in dense layers, reducing resource consumption with minimal performance trade-offs. It operates in three modes: Fixed, applying uniform pruning ratios; Dynamic, enabling layer-specific pruning; and Genetic, employing a genetic algorithm to optimize pruning ratios for accuracy and hardware constraints such as RAM, MAC operations, flash memory, latency, and energy. Experiments on six benchmark datasets show significant resource optimizations with minimal accuracy loss; for example, on the Visual Wake Word dataset, RAM, MACs, Flash memory, latency, and energy usage were reduced by 32%, 82%, 74%, 80%, and 65%, respectively, with only a 3% accuracy drop. The tool is open-source and available at https://github.com/BidyutSaha/GenCPruneX, serving as a valuable TinyML optimization toolkit and supporting broader adoption and further research in resource-efficient TinyML solutions.

articleTitle: Study of 5G NR Network Against Mixed Traffic
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: 5th Generation Mobile Technology (5G) is said to be the future of wireless cellular technology. It was introduced to handle the heavy traffic demand and to provide low latency and high throughput performance. Although it provides better data performance than existing LTE networks, it has a few limitations that restrict its performance. This study evaluates one of the major limitation of 5G called the bufferbloat problem. Bufferbloating occurs when a network has high-speed capabilities yet the end user experiences a significant latency due to many other users sharing the same network, clogging up the buffers. Typically, Active Queue Management (AQM) algorithms have been well known as a potential solution to the issue of Bufferbloat. It evaluates the performance of various AQM algorithms like CoDel, FQ-CoDel, COBALT, PIE, and FQ-PIE in a 5G New Radio network scenario based on RFC 7928. It concludes that Flow Queuing (FQ) AQM algorithms significantly improve the 5G network performance.

articleTitle: HiPer : An XDR Solution for High Performance Compute Clusters using Zeek and Wazuh
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Internet connectivity in high performance computing (HPC) systems like national super-computing facilities increase the risk of security threats. This paper presents HiPer, an end-to-end extended detection and response (XDR) solution, that detects and responds to Internet-based threats in HPC systems. The solution is incorporated into open-source software Zeek and Wazuh, and is successfully deployed at an enterprise.

articleTitle: Enhancing O-RAN’s Intent-based Management Standards for Seamless Cross-Layer Mobility
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: One of the key challenges in 5G (and beyond 5G) networks is to provide seamless service with user mobility, both at application and network layers. In the former, applications need to be migrated between edge sites; while in the latter User Equipment (UE) network service is handed over between 5G cells during handover. Without proper management of synchronization and control mechanisms between these two layers, both these mobility types would result in service interruptions to users. The recent intent-based management specification from the O-RAN alliance could be a step in the direction of seamlessly unifying these two types to ensure service continuity. However, this specification is still in a nascent stage. In this position paper, therefore, we analyze this mobility issue and propose enhancements to the O-RAN specification that can support seamless cross-layer mobility at both application and network layers.

articleTitle: Outage Analysis of Hybrid VLC/Multi-IRS-aided RF Communication System
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid visible light communication (VLC)/ intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided radio-frequency (RF) communication system tailored for indoor communication scenarios. The system uniquely combines a primary VLC link with an IRS-assisted RF backup link to enhance the reliability and coverage. We analyze the performance of the proposed system by deriving the closed-form expressions for outage probability and outage capacity considering a hard-switching scheme. Specifically, the system maintains transmission over the VLC channel until the instantaneous signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) falls below the threshold, at which point it seamlessly transition to the multiple IRS-aided RF system. We utilize Nakagami-m fading to characterize the RF link and Lambertian radiation emission pattern to model the VLC link, ensuring a comprehensive evaluation of the system performance. The derived analytical expressions are validated through extensive Monte-Carlo simulations. The performance comparison confirms the efficiency of the proposed hybrid system, illustrating significant reliability improvements over the traditional VLC system.

articleTitle: Learning Non-cooperative Driving Practices and its Impact on Road Traffic Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Cooperative driving that prioritizes global safety and efficiency over self-interest is crucial in ensuring smooth traffic flow and enhanced road safety. However, experiencing noncooperative driving is common under heterogeneous and chaotic on-road traffic conditions. While non-cooperativeness is often context-dependent and assessed during direct vehicle interactions, it can be inferred through longitudinal analysis of driving patterns from vehicular kinematics data. This behavior not only adversely affects the vehicle itself but also has a cascading impact on nearby vehicles, ultimately disrupting overall traffic flow. In this study, we quantify a vehicle’s non-cooperativeness using kinematic data and further model its cascading effects on nearby cooperative vehicles. Experimental analysis was conducted using the SUMO traffic simulator and the TraCI interface to assess the impact of non-cooperativeness on overall traffic dynamics. This research is among the first to examine the cascading effects of a vehicle’s non-cooperativeness on its cooperative nearby vehicles.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Quantum Image Representations Algorithms for Hybrid-Quantum applications
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This paper examines Quantum Image Representation Algorithms (QIRA), which have significantly advanced the encoding and manipulation of visual data using quantum computing. It explores key developments in image representation techniques, focusing on Flexible Representation of Quantum Images (FRQI), Novel Enhanced Quantum Representation (NEQR), Generalized Quantum Image Representation (GQIR), Bit Plane Representation of Quantum Images (BRQI), and Order Encoding Quantum Image Model (OQIM). Using the Qiskit framework, these methods are implemented to encode classical images into quantum states and perform various quantum operations. The paper provides a comprehensive understanding of QIRA by outlining the background of these representation techniques and rigorously evaluating their performance in image reconstruction. The evaluation is based on metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Cosine Similarity, Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR).

articleTitle: Unveiling the Trade-offs: A Parameter-Centric Comparison of Synchronous and Asynchronous Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a transformative paradigm enabling decentralized model training while preserving data privacy. Within FL, synchronous and asynchronous training modes are two widely adopted approaches. This paper compares synchronous and asynchronous federated learning by examining their impact across accuracy and convergence epochs. Through a series of experimental evaluations, we demonstrate the strengths and limitations of each approach in diverse settings, offering insights into the trade-offs and applicability of synchronous and asynchronous FL modes for various distributed learning scenarios. Our findings aim to guide researchers and practitioners in selecting optimal FL configurations based on their system requirements and performance priorities.

articleTitle: Unlocking Eye Gestures with Earable Inertial Sensing for Accessible HCI
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Eye gestures are widely used in many applications, including device control, biometrics, visual analytics, and health-care, like Alzheimer’s, accessibility, etc. The conventional method for eye gesture detection needs visual information processing devices or smart glasses to capture the movement patterns of the eyeballs. In this paper, we present a novel framework that utilizes inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors embedded in earable devices for real-time eye gesture detection, which can work as a complementary to visual information processing devices. The framework translates specific eye movements into actionable commands, enabling hands-free interaction for users with limited mobility. Through extensive experimentation with 14 participants across diverse activities such as sitting, walking, running, and driving, the framework demonstrated high accuracy in eye gesture recognition, achieving a macro F1 score of 0.85 on our self-collected dataset.

articleTitle: Variational Quantum Factorization (VQF) using Different Variations of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Variational quantum factoring (VQF), a variational quantum algorithm, has been proposed as an alternative to Shor’s algorithm for factoring numbers and has been experimentally implemented to factor numbers much larger than what Shor’s algorithm has factorized thus far. The focus of this work is comparing the performance of different variations of quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) in terms of implementing VQF. Hence, VQF has been implemented here on the Qiskit quantum simulation framework using standard QAOA, multi-angle QAOA (maQAOA), conditional value at risk (CVaR) QAOA, and CVar maQAOA. Using these methods, VQF has been implemented for factorizing bi-prime numbers 143 and 291311 using 4 and 6 qubits respectively, and for factorizing a tri-prime number, 175, using 3 qubits. For factoring of 143 and 175, maQAOA yields the highest success probability numbers (0.92 and 0.99 respectively), while for factoring 291311, CVar maQAOA with 0.75 of the total measurements contributing to the expectation value yields the highest success probability.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Multi-Angle Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (ma-QAOA) Compared to QAOA On Simulation and Experimental Hardware Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Multi-angle quantum approximate optimization algorithm (ma-QAOA) has been proposed as an alternative to regular QAOA for solving optimization problems using noisy intermediate scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. Here, we first implement QAOA and ma-QAOA algorithms to solve MaxCut on weighted and unweighted versions of the Erdős–Rényi (ER) and random cubic (RC) graphs of 6 and 10 nodes. Quantum circuit parameters are updated iteratively through classical feedback with the quantum circuit for forward pass modelled on Qiskit simulator without noise models. Then, the quantum circuit for the final run with updated parameters is implemented on Qiskit simulator without noise models, Qiskit simulator with experimentally benchmarked noise models (fake back-end), and also on actual experimental quantum hardware (IBM’s 127-qubit quantum processor ibm brisbane). We show that for most graph instances, ma-QAOA performs better than QAOA (in terms of approximation ratio (AR)) and needs less stages in the quantum circuit for all three aforementioned methods. Finally, we extend our results up to 14-node RC graphs while restricting ourselves to Qiskit simulation without noise (both for parameter update and final run) and show that for most instances, ma-QAOA again needs much less stages compared to QAOA to obtain reasonable AR.

Author Keywords: Multi- Angled Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (ma-QAOA)

articleTitle: mmWave Based User Identification using Gait Signatures
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: In this work, we present milliGait , a user identification using gait patterns captured by millimeter wave (mmWave) radar technology. milliGait takes into account the unique movement signatures of individuals to enable privacy secured accurate user identification. Using a Commercial-Off-the-self (COTS) mmWave radar we have collected mmWave features, particularly the range information and range-doppler profile features, extracted from the raw I/Q samples. To categorize people according to their leg movement patterns, we developed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model using the mmWave features. The two features namely the range information and the range-doppler profile is fed into two concurrent CNN models (1D and 2D CNN models respectively). Finally a fully-connecyed classifier is employed to identify the subjects. We have evaluated milliGait with 3 different subjects with an authentication accuracy of over 80%.

articleTitle: Osmotic Computing Based Secure Resource Orchestration Scheme for Vehicular Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The advancement in technology leads to provide an efficient communication among vehicles to offload resource-intensive tasks for transportation-based services. However, it may cause issue related to efficient secure resource utilization among vehicular nodes. The key reason behind these considerations are the high mobility of vehicles and their high computational requirements for task execution. To solve these issues, an osmotic computing based vehicular communication scheme has been proposed. The primary objective of the scheme is to provide a communication model which can perform effective secure resource management among static or dynamic vehicular nodes through Osmotic Computing. By utilizing the key components of osmotic computing such as osmotic resource manager and node manager, numerous resources have been shared with the vehicles in an effective way. The performance of the proposed scheme has been evaluated using simulation. Results obtained show that the proposed scheme outperform the existing schemes in terms of various performance evaluation parameters.

articleTitle: Next-Level Intrusion Detection: Multilayered Security for Future Generation 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Gigantic evolution of the communication network from 5G New Radio to 6G displays terabits of data transmitted every day, or hundreds of exabytes. However, it is also associated with numerous challenges such as energy efficiency, data rate, and security menaces. To satisfy such requirements, we propose an intrusion detection methodology based on layer-wise analysis under graph theory representation. The layered analysis reduces the complexity, computational time while maintaining the accuracy, FAR (False Alarm Rate), and detection rate. First, we perform the layered analysis to define vulnerable nodes in the network, one vulnerable node from each layer. Second, we assess the SR (Secrecy Rate) and EE (Energy Efficiency) upper and lower bounds for each vulnerable node. The attained parameters of EE and SR investigated using cross intrusion detection function to spot the attacked node(s).

articleTitle: Deep Digital Twin Services for Personalized MPX Treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: With the advent of smart healthcare services, rapid and automated diagnosis from images of skin lesions is critical to combat fast-spreading viruses such as monkeypox (Mpox or MPX) and significantly improve public health. The recent cases in Thailand reporting a suspected first case on August 21, 2024, and Sweden on August 14, 2024, among others, highlight the pandemic threat of Mpox. This study presents the Deep Digital Twin Services for Personalized Treatment (D2T-PT) model, which combines transfer learning and Digital Twin (DT) technology to improve the accuracy of Mpox detection and real-time monitoring, supported by the Squeeze-and-Excitation Block (SEB) attention mechanism, which opens up new horizons for personalized healthcare. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models were tested on the Monkeypox Skin Lesion Dataset (MSLD), with the advanced adaptive NasNetMobile model achieving excellent results: 100% recall, 98% ROC score, 97.78% accuracy with precision of 95%. This robust model enables physicians to make early and accurate Mpox diagnoses and monitor patient response to treatment in real-time, ultimately helping to contain the spread of the virus.

articleTitle: Real-time Air Quality Monitoring and Context-aware Alert System
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Air quality monitoring is gaining increasing importance as awareness about the health impacts of air pollution continues to grow. These monitors typically track air pollutants to give users a clearer picture of their environment. Accurate and real-time monitoring increases our understanding of the surrounding air we breathe and allows us to improve it. The proposed system helps users minimize their exposure to harmful pollutants by providing real-time data on the concentration of various gases. The system triggers alerts directly to the subscribed user’s mobile phones in case of any hazardous situations so that the user can take appropriate actions immediately to resolve the issue. Our extensive data collection and evaluation with off-the-shelf machine learning models indicated an overall F1-score of 99.54 (±0.5)% with a simple random forest model in classifying burning, cooking, occupancy in a closed room, using aerosol products, based on the sensor’s readings.

articleTitle: Streamlined Data Pipeline for Real-Time Threat Detection and Model Inference
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Real-time threat detection in streaming data is crucial yet challenging due to varying data volumes and speeds. This paper presents an architecture designed to manage large-scale, high-speed data streams using deep learning and machine learning models. The system utilizes Apache Kafka for high-throughput data transfer and a publish-subscribe model to facilitate continuous threat detection. Various machine learning techniques, including XGBoost, Random Forest, and LightGBM, are evaluated to identify the best model for classification. The ExtraTrees model achieves exceptional performance with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score all reaching 99% using the SensorNetGuard dataset within this architecture. The PyFlink framework, with its parallel processing capabilities, supports real-time training and adaptation of these models. The system calculates prediction metrics every 2,000 data points, ensuring efficient and accurate real-time threat detection.

articleTitle: Self Organized Anchor Group based Routing Protocol for IoT Initial Setup
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Geographical routing approach relies on local geographic information and performs multi-hop routing with the help of local decisions. The nodes are represented by 3D coordinates as some real IoT networks may be deployed in high buildings, hilly areas, underground or underwater. The geographical routing protocols follow the greedy path and suffer from void node problem (VNP). The traditional recovery policies follow a longer path around the boundary nodes of the void region which may go out of energy quickly. Thus, this paper proposes the concept of anchor group and presents an efficient anchor group routing protocol (EAGR) for IoT networks. The anchor group is treated as a sub-destination region where a group of nodes behaves like sub-destinations, which bypass the boundary nodes of the void to minimize the path length and divide the network traffic, in case of void in the network. The paper is also focused on considering the residual energy in the contention-based next-hop selection process. The experimental work has been carried out in the OMNET++ simulator’s INET framework and observed that the proposed method is outperforming existing protocols. Moreover, it has reported a longer network lifetime and is able to survive longer than other existing geographical routing protocols on high load.

articleTitle: Quantum Variational Singular Value Decomposition: A new hybrid approach towards quantum image compression
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This research paper explores the application of singular value decomposition (SVD) in quantum image processing (QIP), specifically focusing on the computation of eigenvalues using variational quantum algorithms. SVD is a powerful mathematical tool in image processing, used for tasks such as image compression, noise reduction, and feature extraction. In this study, we propose quantum variational singular value decomposition (QVSVD) based on the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to determine the eigenvalues that contributes in calculating the singular values of the image matrix and eventually doing the SVD. This facilitates the extraction of eigenvalues with exponential speedup on real hardware compared to classical methods. We detail the implementation of this quantum algorithm within the framework of QIP, highlighting its advantages in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy on a Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing (FTQC). Furthermore, we present a comparative analysis of the quantum and the classical method of SVD, demonstrating the accuracy of the image data. The simulation results validate the theoretical advantages of using quantum algorithms for SVD in image processing. This work not only underscores the potential of quantum computing in enhancing image processing techniques but also sets the stage for future research in the field, exploring more complex image processing tasks and other quantum algorithms. Our findings suggest that quantum image processing can offer unprecedented capabilities, paving the way for advancements in various applications such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and multimedia processing.

articleTitle: Phase Shift Optimization for Energy-Efficient Uplink Communication in IRS-Aided System
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This paper examines the integration of Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) in beyond 5G (B5G) communication networks, where the IRS reflects signals with adjustable phase shifts. By optimizing these phase shifts, called passive beamforming, substantial improvements in communication performance can be achieved. We maximize energy efficiency in the uplink communication, utilizing the IRS. However, including an IRS introduces complexities, particularly in channel estimation. To address this, we examine two innovative approaches to minimize the channel estimation overhead: the first leverages a grouping strategy for the reflecting elements. In contrast, the second approach utilizes positioned-based phase optimization. Simulation results confirm that the IRS significantly enhances energy efficiency compared to the traditional system.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Low-cost System for Disaster Locations Detection using ESP32 CAM and TinyML
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, low-power solution for real-time natural disaster or calamity location detection using the ESP32 CAM, a GPS module, and TinyML. By overlaying calamity locations on open-source street maps, our system improves user interaction with spatial data, aiding navigation and safety during disasters. The model achieves 88% accuracy while using minimal RAM and FLASH memory, offering a cost-effective alternative to expensive devices. Additionally, it can be deployed on UAVs, or drones, or towers, for extensive scanning, alerting remote servers or disaster rescue centers upon detection for timely responses.

articleTitle: Sustainable Drone Surveillance System Using Eternal Vertex Cover and Periodic Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), or drones, are transforming surveillance strategies in various fields, including border security and wildlife conservation. Their ability to monitor large, challenging areas in real time has established them as a valuable tool, particularly in scenarios where traditional surveillance methods face operational and logistical limitations. This research focuses on optimizing drone-based surveillance along the International borders, and in wildlife conservation areas, where challenges like illegal crossings, cattle smuggling, and poaching present serious security and economic threats. Leveraging UAVs provides a cost-effective, flexible, and highly deployable solution that overcomes the limitations of static surveillance systems and limited human patrols. We propose an optimized drone-based system designed to enhance operational efficiency, coverage, and adaptability in these complex environments, with potential applications in various sectors requiring comprehensive, real-time surveillance. We propose modeling the problem using the Eternal Vertex Cover problem, a dynamic extension of the classical Vertex Cover problem. Given the NP-hard nature of determining this cover number, our research explores heuristic and algorithmic approaches to achieve an efficient and scalable solution. We also propose an intelligent charging mechanism for the drones for their continuous operation. All proposed approaches are evaluated using randomly generated datasets as long as benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: On Demand Transmissions of Common Signals for Network Energy Saving
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: 5G networks require deployment across multiple frequency bands, often involving more antennas and greater bandwidths, increasing energy consumption and raising concerns for service providers. Reducing network energy usage is essential to promote greener deployments and lower operational costs. Some energy-saving strategies were considered in 5G, however, they are mostly limited to user Equipment (UE) specific signals. Base stations (BS), responsible for transmitting common signals such as Synchronization Signal Block (SSB) and System Information Block 1 (SIB1) for initial UE access, even without active connections, are the primary contributors to energy consumption. Adapting these common operations based on network conditions can significantly reduce BS energy use. This paper explores energy saving techniques of On-demand (OD) downlink transmissions in time and space, addresses gaps in current 5G New Radio (NR) energy-saving methods, and employs the 3GPP energy consumption model to evaluate the effectiveness of proposed strategies.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Dynamic Logging Framework for Cloud Native Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Modern applications, especially those built on microservices, produce large volumes of observability data, with logs accounting for a significant portion of this data, making effective monitoring essential. The widespread deployment of cloud applications has led operations teams to collect excessive data out of “fear of missing out,” resulting in significant costs for storage and analysis. This paper demonstrates a dynamic logging framework proposed in our previous research [1], focusing on when, where, and at what granularity to collect log data. The system selectively captures logs from unhealthy microservices and their neighbors, reducing data collection by 95% while maintaining log quality for downstream downstream AI for IT operations (AIOps) tasks [2], thus facilitating effective fault identification and mitigation.

articleTitle: Use of Channel Occupancy for Multi Link WiFi 7 Scheduler Design in ns-3
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The newest WiFi standard, WiFi 7, has introduced Multi Link Operation (MLO) that enables WiFi devices to utilize multiple links simultaneously (asynchronous mode). This is particularly significant in view of the fact that WiFi network traffic is increasingly multi-class or heterogeneous, implying that future network optimization must simultaneously address multiple Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) - throughput, reliability, latency. Such a feature will enable provisioning for strict latency constraints of new applications like augmented/virtual reality in the presence of (usual) throughput-oriented best-effort traffic. Thus, the availability of MLO naturally leads to innovative MLO scheduler design approaches that aim to appropriately allocate traffic across various links in response to current link state.Network performance evaluation of such new scheduler designs continue to rely heavily on network simulations such as ns-3 (www.nsnam.org). Broadly speaking, there exists a need to expose common heuristics to such MLO schedulers to enable exploration of data-driven, in-simulation MLO optimization approaches. In that spirit, we describe the ns-3 implementation of the channel occupancy (CO) metric, intended to serve as a measure of link congestion. We validated our implementation by comparing against appropriate analytical models and subsequently suggest approaches to novel MLO scheduler designs that utilize CO, via a few illustrative examples.

articleTitle: Drone-Assisted Load Distribution Framework for Traffic Optimization in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Device connectivity has been redefined by the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) technology, enabling diverse applications in areas such as smart cities, smart homes, and healthcare. These applications produce massive amounts of data, making it a significant challenge to offload tasks to cloud servers. However, the physical distance between devices often leads to latency issues for IoT systems, impacting time-sensitive applications. Fog computing tackles this issue by processing data closer to IoT devices. However, a high user density can strain the capacity of a macro base station, potentially leading to congestion. Drone Base Stations (DBSs) provide a flexible solution by acting as mobile relays to reduce latency and traffic burden. To address this issue, this work proposes a drone-assisted load distribution strategy in IoT networks. In our proposed approach, we deploy DBS efficiently using a greedy optimization technique. However, after the deployment of DBS, an optimal base station assignment framework dynamically connects user equipment to the most suitable base station, helping to minimize latency and enhance network performance. This dual-phase approach provides a scalable and practical solution for realtime IoT applications.
